questions.title: Core clinical parameters to identify moderate-severe AD with head and neck involvement
questions.text: Clinicians should use scoring systems that have specific criteria for the face and neck region, such as EASI, in addition to more global and holistic scores like HADS, PPNRS, DLQI etc, when evaluating patients with AD with head and neck involvement
questions.section: Clinical challenges in managing head and neck AD / Core clinical parameters to identify moderate-severe AD with head and neck involvement

questions.title: Core clinical parameters to identify moderate-severe AD with head and neck involvement

questions.title: Main challenges and pitfalls with current treatment options in H&N AD
questions.text: While topical corticosteroids are offered as a first-line treatment for AD with head and neck involvement in-line with current guidance, earlier optimisation of systemic or targeted therapies may be appropriate in selected patients with significant head and neck involvement
questions.section: Current treatment pathways for head and neck AD and their limitations / Main challenges and pitfalls with current treatment options in H&N AD

questions.title: Main challenges and pitfalls with current treatment options in H&N AD
questions.text: Arbitrary local EASI cut-offs and regional variations in commissioning criteria fail to account for the disproportionate impact of head and neck AD, leading to systemic undertreatment of patients who otherwise meet national systemic therapy guidelines

questions.title: Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD
questions.text: Patch testing and review of the original diagnosis should be considered when new head and neck symptoms arise from treatments used for existing AD
questions.section: Current treatment pathways for head and neck AD and their limitations / Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD

questions.title: Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD
questions.text: Oral antifungal therapy should be employed for head and neck AD flares when clinical signs and symptoms, such as refractory facial erythema, scaling, and severe itching suggest secondary yeast involvement or a Malassezia driving phenotype
questions.section: Current treatment pathways for head and neck AD and their limitations / Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD

questions.title: Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD
questions.text: Topical treatments should be utilised to manage head and neck flares that present as paradoxical redness or residual disease despite successful systemic therapy
questions.section: Current treatment pathways for head and neck AD and their limitations / Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD

questions.title: Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD
questions.text: A switch to an alternative biologic or a JAK inhibitor may be considered when head and neck flares present as paradoxical redness or residual disease that fails to respond to topical interventions during existing systemic therapy
questions.section: Current treatment pathways for head and neck AD and their limitations / Management of new symptoms or “flare-ups” that arise from treatments for existing AD

questions.title: Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement
questions.text: Improved guidance for the identification of AD with head and neck involvement should include more specific screening and evaluation tools for use across different skin tones
questions.section: Defining priorities to address unmet needs in head and neck AD / Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement

questions.title: Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement
questions.text: Improved guidance for the management of AD with head and neck involvement should include practical management advice, such as which tests to perform and when and general skin care advice
questions.section: Defining priorities to address unmet needs in head and neck AD / Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement

questions.title: Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement
questions.text: Improved guidance for the management of moderate-severe AD with head and neck involvement should include first-line recommendations for targeted treatments of the head and neck region, based on patient groups, contraindications, and severity of the disease
questions.section: Defining priorities to address unmet needs in head and neck AD / Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement

questions.title: Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement
questions.text: AD with head and neck involvement represents a clinically meaningful presentation with specific challenges characterised by increased disease burden, treatment resistance, and the need for tailored management approaches
questions.section: Defining priorities to address unmet needs in head and neck AD / Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement

questions.title: Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement
questions.text: AD with head and neck involvement should be defined using the Hannifin and Rajka criteria (with patients having >3 major and/or minor symptoms, including itch, erythema, scaling oedema, lichenification or photosensitivity), with the disease affecting the eyelids, cheeks, scalp, or neck
questions.section: Defining priorities to address unmet needs in head and neck AD / Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement

questions.title: Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement
questions.text: Management of AD with head and neck involvement should include consideration of psychological comorbidities and appropriate support or referral where needed
questions.section: Defining priorities to address unmet needs in head and neck AD / Guidance for AD with head and neck involvement

IntroductionFollowing a Delphi consensus, the aim of this project is to build consensus to improve the clinical management of atopic dermatitis (AD) with head and neck (H&N) involvement.
To help us achieve this, we are inviting you to review the first round of consensus statements that were developed by a panel of experts forming a steering committee (hereafter referred to as the expert committee) of healthcare professionals, based on an initial evidence review.
This double blinded project has been initiated and funded by a pharmaceutical company and is being managed and delivered by Triducive Partners Ltd (an independent specialist healthcare consultancy). We are required by the General Data Protection Regulation to reveal the name of the sponsoring company, and do not intend that this should influence you in any way. We will share this information at the end of the survey.
This is a closed question survey, and the purpose is to measure level of agreement with the consensus statements.
Consent for participation will be implied by completion of the survey. The information provided by the participants will be used for the stated specified purposes only. An individual's responses will not be used in any way that would allow their identification. All completed questionnaires will be collected by M3 Global, a market research organisation, and analysed by Triducive. Anonymous responses will be provided in an aggregated form to the expert panel and sponsoring company.
For further information about how Triducive protects your personal information and how you may exercise your data protection rights, you can contact Triducive at info@triducive.com or visit https://triducive.com/privacy-policy/.
